place.source_title: J. Gerken Building (now U.S. Post Office), Main Street

brief: Two-storey red-brick nineteenth-century commercial block reused as the village post office: a corbelled and dentilled brick cornice with a name panel, a row of seven tall round-arched upper windows, and a cast-iron storefront of slender columns with display windows, a recessed door and transoms; a flagpole, bench and highway route sign on the sidewalk in a small declining river town.

facade.notes: the J. Gerken Building (Henderson MN, 1885), now the post office: a two-storey red-brick commercial block with a corbelled, dentilled cornice and name panel, segmental-arched upper windows, a cast-iron storefront with transoms; flags, a bench, a highway marker, a pickup at the curb

why.note: a small town's post office leases an old store block on Main Street
